title: Impact of Compulsory Schooling on Wages

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Instrumental Variables (IV) estimation using Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS). The compulsory schooling year (z) serves as an instrument for years of education (x) to identify the causal effect on log wages (y). Key assumptions: (1) Relevance - compulsory schooling laws affect educational attainment, (2) Exclusion restriction - compulsory schooling laws only affect wages through their impact on education, and (3) Monotonicity - the instrument affects education in the same direction for all individuals.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s68_data.csv")

# Display basic summary statistics
cat("Summary Statistics:\n")
print(summary(data))
cat("\n")

# First stage regression (relevance check)
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
cat("First Stage Results (Education on Instrument):\n")
print(summary(first_stage))
cat("\nFirst Stage F-statistic:", summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1], "\n\n")

# Check instrument strength (F-stat > 10 rule of thumb)
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
cat("Instrument strength check: F-statistic =", f_stat, 
    ifelse(f_stat > 10, "(Strong instrument)", "(Weak instrument)"), "\n\n")

# OLS estimation (for comparison)
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
cat("OLS Results (potentially biased):\n")
print(summary(ols_model))
cat("OLS coefficient on education:", coef(ols_model)[2], "\n\n")

# 2SLS IV estimation
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
cat("IV (2SLS) Results:\n")
print(summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE))

# Extract key coefficient
iv_coef <- coef(iv_model)[2]
iv_se <- summary(iv_model)$coefficients[2, 2]
cat("\nMain Result - IV coefficient on education:", iv_coef, "\n")
cat("Standard error:", iv_se, "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: [", iv_coef - 1.96*iv_se, ",", iv_coef + 1.96*iv_se, "]\n\n")

# Robustness check 1: Reduced form (direct effect of instrument on outcome)
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
cat("Reduced Form Results (Direct effect of instrument on wages):\n")
print(summary(reduced_form))
cat("Reduced form coefficient:", coef(reduced_form)[2], "\n\n")

# Robustness check 2: Compare IV and OLS
cat("Comparison of Estimates:\n")
cat("OLS coefficient:", coef(ols_model)[2], "\n")
cat("IV coefficient:", iv_coef, "\n")
cat("Difference (IV - OLS):", iv_coef - coef(ols_model)[2], "\n\n")

# Robustness check 3: Test for endogeneity (Hausman test)
hausman_test <- summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)$diagnostics
cat("Hausman Test for Endogeneity:\n")
print(hausman_test["Wu-Hausman",])
cat("\n")

# Simple correlation check
cat("Correlations:\n")
cat("Education-Instrument correlation:", cor(data$x, data$z), "\n")
cat("Wages-Education correlation:", cor(data$y, data$x), "\n")
cat("Wages-Instrument correlation:", cor(data$y, data$z), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient on education (around 0.08-0.15), indicating that an additional year of education increases log wages by approximately 8-15%. The IV estimate should be larger than the OLS estimate due to measurement error bias in education and potential ability bias that causes OLS to underestimate the true causal effect. The compulsory schooling instrument typically captures returns to education for individuals at the margin of compliance, which may represent higher local average treatment effects for those who would not otherwise continue their education.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use compulsory schooling year as an instrument for education.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis suggests that additional compulsory schooling has a negative impact on log wages.
